title: General deep-page retrieval limitation — what is now reusable, and what remains outside the repository

priorRecords.status: both reports read end to end; bytes, sha256, page locators and extracts complete
priorRecords.treatment: PRESERVED BYTE-IDENTICAL — re-verified by this bundle, not superseded
PRESERVED — the cap it recorded is the limitation this item describes
PRESERVED — the class REPORTED_NOT_READ now has a name in the contract

determination.openBecause: the repository-controlled half is now reusable and tested; the fetch and extraction half still depends on an environment with egress and PDF tooling, and on issuer/exchange provider access — both outside this repository
determination.whatChanged: a retrieval-evidence contract, a bundle reader and a CLI gate now exist in the repository, and the WI-6A-S2 bundle verifies against them offline; a fabricated claim is refused with named violations
determination.whatDidNotChange: no new retrieval was performed; the in-process ~55-printed-page reader cap is unchanged; two-up column relationships are still not resolved by extraction

residualItems.finding: Every in-process reader available to the work item stops at a printed-page cap (~55 printed pages on the FY24 report, ~32 on FY23).
residualItems.iidImpact: a disclosure printed beyond the cap cannot be read in-process, so it cannot be cited, and its absence cannot be concluded
residualItems.nextPath: a reader that returns whole documents, or a retrieval harness in an environment with egress and PDF tooling

residualItems.finding: From this environment the issuer, both exchanges, the annual-report host and the Wayback Machine all abort TLS before any HTTP status; only an allowlisted host answers.
residualItems.iidImpact: no primary-source retrieval is possible here; nothing may be read, and nothing may be reported as absent
residualItems.nextPath: retrieval executed in an environment with egress (as WI-6A-S2 did out-of-process), with the record kept in-repository

residualItems.finding: No PDF extraction tooling exists in this environment (no poppler/qpdf/mutool/ghostscript, no pypdf/pdfminer/fitz).
residualItems.iidImpact: page text cannot be produced here, so page provenance has to be carried in from an out-of-process extraction and then verified
residualItems.nextPath: pinned extraction in the retrieval harness; the verifier already checks what it produces

residualItems.finding: Each bundle carried a bespoke guard test, so retrieval evidence was not checkable generically: a bundle could cite an unextracted page, quote a refused fetch, renumber a printed page, or claim a complete read of three pages.
residualItems.iidImpact: a fabricated or drifted deep-page claim could have reached a finding unchallenged
residualItems.resolution: closed-vocabulary contract + bundle reader + CLI gate + 22 targeted tests, verified on the real S2 bundle and on a negative control

residualItems.finding: The only successful deep read used a temporary GitHub Actions workflow, visible in public run logs and then deleted, so the capability was never a reviewable artifact of the repository.
residualItems.iidImpact: the retrieval cannot be repeated by a reviewer, so its result rests on a record rather than on a method
residualItems.nextPath: a committed, reviewable retrieval harness with pinned extraction; deliberately not added here (no new persistence mechanism, and the harness must run where egress exists)

residualItems.finding: Printed page numbers, PDF page indices and two-up sheets can diverge; a renumbered page or a sheet mapped twice could pass unnoticed.
residualItems.iidImpact: a quotation could be attributed to a page that does not carry it
residualItems.resolution: the extract header, the page map, the document record and the quotation are cross-checked; drift in any one of them is a named violation

residualItems.finding: On a two-up sheet the layout-preserving extractor interleaves the two printed columns line by line, so table, caption and note relationships are not reconstructed.
residualItems.iidImpact: a multi-column table cannot be read as rows from such an extract; the standing rule is that a two-up sheet is never quoted as a single row
residualItems.nextPath: column-aware extraction (cut the sheet in half before text order is applied), then the same verifier applies unchanged

residualItems.finding: Retrieval failure and genuine absence were separated only by prose; a refused fetch could in principle have been read as an empty page.
evidence: iips-platform/tests/investment/retrieval-evidence.test.ts (a bundle of failed retrievals reports zero retrieved)
residualItems.iidImpact: L-037s own rule — absence of wording beyond the cap is not evidence of absence — is now mechanical rather than editorial
residualItems.resolution: closed status vocabulary; READ quotation refused on any non-RETRIEVED document; REPORTED_NOT_READ never counted as read; a bundle of failures reports zero retrieved

residualItems.finding: For Zensar the deep pages were read: both consolidated Note 27 sentences at printed pp.304-305 and pp.320-321, with bytes, sha256, page locators and committed extracts.
residualItems.iidImpact: that issuer and that filing are not an open retrieval question; this item is about the class, not about Zensar
residualItems.resolution: re-verified by runs/01-s2-verification.txt in this bundle

nextResolutionPath: commit a retrieval harness (pinned tooling, reviewable, no temporary workflow) that runs where egress exists
have the harness emit exactly source-bytes.json / page-map.json / quotes-verified.json + provenance-headed extracts, which this gate already verifies
add column-aware extraction for two-up sheets, then re-verify the same bundles unchanged
notClaimed: that the retrieval class is closed
